label: GO step after an unrewarded trial, early in the episode (stronger before a1 choices)
explanation: Fires only at GO (100% of activation mass; essentially never at D1 or D2). Within GO it depends mainly on the previous trial being unrewarded (91% of mass; rate 11% vs 1.6% after reward) and on episode time: the rate falls steadily from 15% in trials 0-9 to under 1% after trial 70, and it is near zero on the episode first trial. It is stronger when the agent is about to choose a1 (model_act a1: rate 22% vs 9% for a2; 70% of mass), when the good state is S1, and when the value head output is mid-high (7.7 to 8.1). It is silent when value > 8.1. Predicate GO & prev unrewarded & ep_trial < 50 gives dev F1 0.58, mass recall 0.84; adding the upcoming choice a1 raises precision but loses recall. False positives are mostly unrewarded GO steps before a2 choices; misses are mostly weak a1 GO steps after rewarded trials, or later in the episode. The tie to time-in-episode suggests the unit is graded (magnitude reflecting early-episode uncertainty or lack of reward) rather than a clean binary detector. Uses only observed variables plus the agent own upcoming choice.
